review_type: independent stage and runtime visual review
readiness_decision: Useful polished prototype; the frozen stage remains below the 9/10 source-fidelity target. The large ramp-shadow defect is resolved and vapor is substantially improved. Remaining issues are smaller: airborne car cast-shadow sharpness, layered flat bases in atlas vapor, and simplified apron light/material detail.

included: Ramp silhouette, structure, deck and paint
Jets and vapor appearance including landing occlusion and 13s clearance
excluded: Car model form and author repair quality
scope.method: Fresh reads of all 17 immutable V5 runtime captures, the four-puff atlas, five actual source frames, and stage/effects code for cause. No app automation, live camera changes, app/source edits, or consultation of another judge report.

mismatches.disposition: Expected independent model-author edits; model quality excluded. Frozen capture images remain valid.

hash_evidence.note: All 17 image hashes and all non-model stage/effect/texture/code entries matched initially. This judgment applies to the frozen capture state, not subsequent live car repairs.

confirmed_improvements.evidence: Ready, wide and overhead no longer have the black C-shaped ramp/truss projection that dominated V3. The ramp remains grounded visually by its foot and stage light pool.

The new atlas produces coarse irregular lobes, sharp wisps, internal blue-gray shade and darker aged areas, replacing the smooth bright wall. Landing remains substantially occluded in landscape and portrait.

The car is plainly visible left of the cloud. The trailing cloud still exists, while its left edge becomes darker/translucent. This follows the source-supported idea of a large persistent vapor mass rather than erasing it.
Ramp stripe remains continuous in show/portrait release, deck is visible, brace rhythm is consistent, floor fade is much less obtrusive than V2, and portrait/full-path framing remains sound.

remaining_material_gaps.evidence: The high ramp shadow is gone, but the airborne car still makes a crisp near-black isolated footprint on the floor. It is small in show view and conspicuous in overhead. This is a rendering/lighting issue, separate from car-model form.
remaining_material_gaps.fix: Fade or disable distant car cast shadow as height increases, and retain a soft short contact shadow when grounded. Check overhead, release, ready and landing so the car does not lose contact grounding.
remaining_material_gaps.source_caveat: Source lights and camera differ, so exact shadow position is not expected; the issue is the detached hard black cutout.

remaining_material_gaps.evidence: The atlas is a strong improvement, but many sprites contain complete upright cloud masses with flat ground-like bases. When billboard particles overlap at different heights, the lower cloud shows horizontal shelf/strip edges and similarly scaled repeated cauliflower forms. This reads as stacked images in parts of descent/landing. The actual source has soft ground spread plus rising lobes with less regular internal detail. At 13s the aged cloud is improved and no longer a uniformly bright rounded capsule.
remaining_material_gaps.fix: Reserve complete flat-base puffs for ground level. For elevated particles, soften their lower edge or use wisps/open-bottom variants, vary the vertical size/arrangement more, and reduce repeated similarly sized full-cloud silhouettes. Keep the useful blue-gray interior, local touchdown opacity, and visible car at 13s.
remaining_material_gaps.source_caveat: Large persistent vapor is supported by frames_24 and _26. A different turbulent silhouette alone is not a defect; the remaining concern is visible sprite construction.

remaining_material_gaps.evidence: The stage still has very regular identical cool spot pools, clean bright rectangular lenses, a nearly textureless black apron and parallel red rails. Actual wide_17 and overhead-37 show grazing reflected light, rough floor variation, white apron/track markings and more uneven brightness/red spill. The main source stage language is present, but the current rendering remains visibly simplified.
remaining_material_gaps.fix: For a further source-fidelity pass, add source-supported dim white apron/track markings and subtle rough grazing reflections, and vary a few bank intensities/aims. Do not increase global fill or add unrelated props.
remaining_material_gaps.source_caveat: The event contains cameras, vehicles and other equipment outside this stage scope; their omission is not scored as a defect.

minor_finish.evidence: The far-end floor still converges to a slightly different black than the background, leaving a faint straight transition in full-path wide-end. It is minor compared with the old bright floor island.
minor_finish.fix: Fade to the exact scene background color rather than pure black.

minor_finish.evidence: The bottom-right control panel is functional and does not hide the supplied active car region, but its persistent block and tiny supporting text are visually heavy for a clean replay. This is secondary to stage fidelity.
minor_finish.fix: Optional compact/collapsible playback controls for a presentation mode.

do_not_regress: Keep the large ramp cast shadow disabled or appropriately softened.
Keep thin noisy pressure jets; do not restore solid opaque cyan cones.
Keep the new cloud lobes/interior shading and age opacity decay.
Keep touchdown cloud occlusion and a visible car at 13 seconds.
Keep portrait action framing and the full-path wide option; tiny actor size at the far end is the natural coverage tradeoff.
Do not treat car-model repairs or fitted numerical motion as stage-quality credit.
limitations: No motion video was supplied for this freeze, so temporal billboard behavior, sorting, popping and cloud coherence are not established.
No direct 10.0s pressure-column capture isolates the stronger source thrust phase; the supplied 9.5s thin jets remain plausible.
The overhead view shows the outer/back face of the upper ramp; absent center paint there is not counted as a new paint bug.
The atlas is an appearance asset; it provides no physical plume measurement or source-motion validation.
conclusion: V5 is materially better than V3 and is suitable as a strong prototype stage. It scores 8.6/10 on the same source-fidelity bar; residual shadow, sprite construction and apron rendering gaps prevent 9/10 approval. No critical functional stage issue was found in the supplied still evidence.
